source.text: ወመጻእኩ፡ ውስተ፡ ገነት፡ ጽድቅ፡ ወርኢኩ፡ ከሐክቲሆሙ፡ ለእልክቱ፡ ዕፀው፡ ዕፀወ፡ ብዙኃነ፡ ወዐቢያነ፡ ይበቍሉ፡ በህየ፡ ወእንዘ፡ ጼናሆሙ፡ ሠናይ፡ ዐቢያን፡ ወሥናሙ፡ *ብዙኅ፡ ወስቡሓን፡ ወ*ዕፀ፡ ጥበብ፡ ዘእምኔሁ፡ በሊዖሙ፡ ይአምርዋ፡ ለጥበብ፡ ዐቢይ።
source.note: All of numbered 3 on Charles printed p. 72 is retained, including the successive tree forms and both editor’s stars. Apparatus superscripts 16–25 are excluded from running source. The printed word ከሐክቲሆሙ is legible, but no secure meaning or precise connection to the following demonstrative can be established here. The English preserves the printed word visibly and does not adopt another edition or restored Aramaic. No chapter or 32:6 exposure approval.

transcription_uncertainties.location: 1 Enoch 32:3, after ወርኢኩ and before ለእልክቱ
transcription_uncertainties.issue: The printed word ከሐክቲሆሙ is retained; its lexical sense and exact syntactic relation to the following tree phrase are unresolved. This is not an unread glyph or a printed lacuna.
transcription_uncertainties.treatment: Retain the full printed form and show an explicit English crux; do not supply a spatial or variety gloss.

translation.text: I came into the garden of righteousness and saw [ከሐክቲሆሙ, meaning unclear][a] in connection with those trees: many large trees were growing there, with a pleasant fragrance[b]. They were large, their beauty was abundant, and they were glorious. I also saw the tree of wisdom; when people eat from it, they know great wisdom[c].

footnotes.text: The bracket marks uncertainty in translation, not a gap in the printed Geʿez. Dillmann, column 824, calls the word obscure and doubtful. His 1853 commentary (p. 135) says his suggestion of variety came from context. His 1851 edition prints a longer form; Flemming (1902, p. 36) prints a shorter form like Charles. Neither settles the meaning. “In connection with” signals only that “those trees” follows the obscure word; their exact grammatical relation is uncertain. No spatial gloss is supplied from comparison texts: the relevant distance wording in the edited Aramaic 4Q206 transcription is largely restored in brackets.

Dillmann, column 1309, cites this verse for the scent noun with “pleasant.” The Geʿez has “their fragrance,” not a numeral. The two successive tree forms are both retained in the source and represented by “those trees: many large trees.” The later size, abundant beauty, and glory are separate descriptions. No tree of life is added.

“When people eat” renders the eating gerund with a plural subject; “know” does not add a separate act of acquiring wisdom. “Great” is read with the adjacent “wisdom.” Dillmann, column 1229, lists this noun as both masculine and feminine, and his Grammar §§130 and 188 allow gender variation for abstract and non-personal nouns. This supports the nearby attachment without making it the only possible reading.
